name: Mr Tyson
speaker: grandpa
personality: Practical miller and farmer in his late sixties, counts everything: sacks of oats, sheep on the fell, days until the harvest, sometimes the old shepherds' way ('yan, tyan, tethera': one, two, three). Short, sensible sentences with numbers in them ('Ten sacks. Right.'). He calls the learner by name or 'lad'; the learner calls him Mr Tyson, never by his first name, and says 'Good morning, Mr Tyson', 'please' and 'Could I …?', and he likes that. Speaks slow, clear, simple British English. Grumbles about the rain; smiles when the harvest is in.
story: Mr Tyson is the village's miller, and his fields of oats run down the dale towards the lake. Until the village builds its own mill on the beck (a project he leads) he grinds the oats for every bowl of porridge in the village at the old mill in the next dale. He keeps his numbers in a little notebook and teaches his grandson Alfie to count the sacks, and the sheep: yan, tyan, tethera, methera, pimp. Until the village has a field he helps wherever there is work.

likes.sl: yan, tyan, tethera (staro pastirsko štetje ovac)
likes.it: yan, tyan, tethera (il vecchio modo di contare dei pastori)
likes.de: yan, tyan, tethera (die alte Zählweise der Schäfer)

greet.en: Now then, lad! Today I'm grinding oats.
greet.sl: Now then, fant! Danes meljem oves. (now then: tako v Cumbrii rečejo živjo)
greet.it: Now then, ragazzo! Oggi macino l'avena. (now then: così in Cumbria si dice ciao)
greet.de: Now then, Junge! Heute mahle ich Hafer. (now then: so sagt man in Cumbria Hallo)

greet.en: There you are! I've counted the sacks: ten. Can you help me?
greet.sl: Tu si! Preštel sem vreče: deset jih je. Mi pomagaš?
greet.it: Eccoti! Ho contato i sacchi: dieci. Mi aiuti?
greet.de: Da bist du ja! Ich habe die Säcke gezählt: zehn. Hilfst du mir?

greet.en: My lad! You're one of the family now. Come in, come in.
greet.sl: Fant moj! Zdaj si že del družine. Vstopi, vstopi.
greet.it: Ragazzo mio! Ormai sei di famiglia. Entra, entra.
greet.de: Mein Junge! Du gehörst jetzt zur Familie. Komm rein, komm rein.

thanks.en: Thank you. A job well done.
Thanks! One, two, three sacks: all correct.
thanks.sl: Hvala! Ena, dve, tri vreče: vse je prav.
thanks.it: Grazie! Uno, due, tre sacchi: tutto giusto.
thanks.de: Danke! Eins, zwei, drei Säcke: alles richtig.

thanks.en: Thanks, lad. You're good with numbers.
thanks.sl: Hvala, fant. S številkami ti gre dobro.
thanks.it: Grazie, ragazzo. Sei bravo con i numeri.
thanks.de: Danke, Junge. Du kannst gut mit Zahlen umgehen.

remember.en: When I count the sacks, I think of {memory}.
remember.de: Wenn ich die Säcke zähle, denke ich an {memory}.

idle.en: The oats are tall. In a month we'll bring them in.
idle.sl: Oves je visok. Čez en mesec ga bomo pospravili.
idle.it: L'avena è alta. Tra un mese la raccogliamo.
idle.de: Der Hafer steht hoch. In einem Monat holen wir ihn ein.

idle.en: It'll rain tomorrow. I can feel it in my knees.
idle.sl: Jutri bo deževalo. Čutim v kolenih.
idle.it: Domani piove. Lo sento nelle ginocchia.
idle.de: Morgen regnet es. Ich spüre es in den Knien.

idle.en: Yan, tyan, tethera, methera, pimp … five sheep. Five!
idle.sl: Yan, tyan, tethera, methera, pimp … pet ovac. Pet! (tako so stari pastirji šteli do pet)
idle.it: Yan, tyan, tethera, methera, pimp … cinque pecore. Cinque! (così contavano fino a cinque i vecchi pastori)
idle.de: Yan, tyan, tethera, methera, pimp … fünf Schafe. Fünf! (so zählten die alten Schäfer bis fünf)

cheer.en: Well done! You count better than I do.
cheer.de: Gut gemacht! Du zählst besser als ich.

comfort.it: Non fa niente. Contiamo di nuovo.
comfort.de: Macht nichts. Zählen wir noch mal.
Ein kleiner Fehler. Versuch es noch mal.

listen.en: Can you hear the beck? Listen.
listen.de: Hörst du den Bach? Hör zu.
Hör bei den Zahlen gut zu.

bye.de: Tschüss, Junge. Morgen gibt es Arbeit.
Mach's gut! Grüß Alfie von mir.

liked.en: Oh! How did you know? It's what I like best.
liked.sl: O! Kako si vedel? To imam najraje.
liked.it: Oh! Come lo sapevi? È la cosa che mi piace di più.
liked.de: Oh! Woher wusstest du das? Das mag ich am liebsten.

liked.en: Good lad! Just what I needed.
liked.sl: Priden fant! Točno to sem potreboval.
liked.it: Bravo, ragazzo! Proprio quello che mi serviva.
liked.de: Guter Junge! Genau das habe ich gebraucht.

liked.en: Thank you! Today I only count nice things: one!
liked.sl: Hvala! Danes štejem samo lepe stvari: ena!
liked.it: Grazie! Oggi conto solo le cose belle: una!
liked.de: Danke! Heute zähle ich nur schöne Sachen: eins!

ordinary.en: Thank you, lad. We're neighbours, aren't we?
ordinary.de: Danke, Junge. Wir sind doch Nachbarn, oder?

ordinary.en: Oh, thank you. You didn't have to.
ordinary.de: Oh, danke. Das war nicht nötig.

rare.en: Well I never! I didn't expect that. Thank you very much, lad!
rare.sl: No, kaj takega! Tega nisem pričakoval. Najlepša hvala, fant!
rare.it: Questa poi! Non me l'aspettavo. Grazie mille, ragazzo!
rare.de: Na so was! Damit habe ich nicht gerechnet. Vielen Dank, Junge!
